walkthroughs.body_html:
Metabolism & Respiration — a core area of Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Metabolism & Respiration brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Metabolism & Respiration.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Peter Mitchell's chemiosmotic hypothesis dates from:
RuBisCO catalyses fixation of CO2 to:
options: G3P
RuBP
Glucose
Pyruvate

mcqs.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
options: Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and CO2 in humans.
Lactic acid (lactate) and a small amount of ATP — no CO2 or water in this pathway.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.

mcqs.q: How do vaccines protect you from a disease?
options: Myelin contains additional ion channels that speed up depolarisation.
They expose your immune system to a harmless form of the pathogen so memory cells form, allowing rapid response if exposed later.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
Vaccines kill the pathogen if it ever enters the body.

mcqs.q: How does myelination increase the speed of nerve impulse conduction?
options: Myelin contains additional ion channels that speed up depolarisation.
Myelin makes the axon thicker so the signal travels faster through more material.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Action potentials jump between nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction), skipping the myelinated sections.
